Comfortable ride: Rides well over bad roads and feels stable at high speeds.
Looks and feels premium: Contemporary looks and material choices inside make it feel more expensive than it is.

Battery warranty: Bigger battery gets a 15 year warranty which offers peace of mind.
cons: Boot space: Limited space in the boot is only enough for two cabin sized trolleys and a laptop bag.
No paddle shifters: Regenerative mode has to be changed via the buttons on the central console which doesn’t feel intuitive.
Fit and finish: Panel gaps and inconsistent plastic panels take away from the premium experience.

pros: Effortless engine: The proven 2.8-litre diesel is torquey and relaxed, now paired with a smoother, more polished automatic.
Big cabin upgrade: A completely redesigned, chunky dashboard and a far more comfortable, big-person-friendly driving position.
Improved ride comfort: Toyota has taken a good amount of sharpness out of the ride, most noticeably in the front row.
Serious off-road hardware: Ladder-frame chassis, low-range 4x4, rear diff lock and a full suite of traction electronics.
Modern, imposing design: The redesigned face and brawnier stance look fresher and more aggressive without losing the Hilux's tough character.
cons: Under-equipped for the price: Manual AC, a manual-dimming mirror, fabric seats and no ADAS on a truck costing around Rs 35-40 lakh on-road.
Compromised rear seat: An upright, non-reclining backrest, a high floor and no rear AC vents make the back bench a poor place for family.
Still firm over big hits: Sharp speed breakers and deep potholes still send a strong jolt through the cabin.
Bulky in the city: Heavy low-speed steering and a 5,325 mm length make tight traffic and parking a chore.
